purpose: Cross-hub bridge graph for the public artifact hubs modeled here (owner-directed 2026-06-06). Encodes how context, skills, tools, MCP connectivity, compression, benchmarks, and harnesses relate and flow into Teleon + Baltor, and asserts the governance rule: NONE of the open hubs is a truth authority — Baltor governs context, Teleon runs capabilities. Read by scripts/check_open_hubs_bridge_graph.py.
relationship_chain: OpenContextHub supplies context → OpenSkillsHub teaches how → OpenToolsHub gives execution → OpenMCPHub connects tools → OpenCompressionHub makes context cheap → OpenBenchmarkHub defines what good means → OpenHubForAI proves it → Teleon runs and evolves → Baltor governs truth → AI Done Right coordinates the portfolio
governance_rule: An open-hub artifact is a reference/candidate, never served truth: discovery is not trust, similarity is not equivalence, output is not truth. Teleon consumes artifacts; Baltor governs whether context becomes verified, reconciled, current, and served.

boundary_laws.benchmark_vs_harness: OpenBenchmarkHub defines WHAT to measure (benchmarks/metrics/datasets/results/suitability); OpenHubForAI runs HOW (harnesses/runners/rubrics/fixtures/conformance). NEVER merged.
boundary_laws.benchmark_result_note: A benchmark result is EVIDENCE, not authority. It cannot by itself promote a Teleon candidate or become Baltor truth; promotion still requires policy gates + receipts + source handles + task-specific scorecards + redteam.
boundary_laws.mcp_discovery_not_trust: OpenMCPHub discovery/metadata is NOT trust; MCP execution is gated through Teleon/OpenTools policy + risk/conformance.
boundary_laws.compression_must_preserve_fidelity: OpenCompressionHub: token savings are INVALID unless answer-critical facts, source handles, held-out warnings, receipts, and tenant scope all survive.
